reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that in-flight oxidation occurs and that annealing at 800 °C causes phase transformations in this HEA, but it provides no data on the use of an inert shielding gas, no demonstration of a resulting oxidation-resistant barrier, and no tests on Zr-alloy cladding. The key premises about the shielding gas, the barrier mechanism, and the comparative performance on cladding are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: In-flight oxidation of FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3 during HVOF spraying influences phase composition and properties
Isothermal annealing at 800 °C transforms the as-sprayed structure into a different phase assemblage
An inert shielding gas can control in-flight oxidation during HVOF spraying of this HEA
Controlled in-flight oxidation plus annealing yields a dense, oxidation-resistant microstructure that acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier
The resulting coating reduces oxygen penetration and weight gain on Zr-alloy cladding relative to uncoated or conventionally coated cladding
